subject: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: you’re validating model quality (hallucination rate, factuality, safety) across our hosted API vs Hyperscaler X and Y for your knowledge-centered agent. Performance (latency) is secondary for this phase; quality/regressions are the gating factor.
- Immediate asks from Acme: a) reproducible eval prompts, b) a small regression check run on a ~500 prompt sample, c) guidance on configs (temperature, max tokens, decode strategy) that align to your current baseline.

Next steps we propose: 
1) We’ll send a CSV of the eval prompts we discussed and a short runbook for how to reproduce the tests (attached).
2) Rishi will set up a short benchmark run against our hosted endpoint and share the regression-check PDF.
3) If results look good, we’ll schedule a live side-by-side test (45m) with your ML lead and our SRE to validate configs and KV/prefix caching behavior.

Proposed timing: we can deliver the prompt CSV and initial regression PDF by Tue EOD 4/19. Can you confirm who on your side will run the comparator tests and whether we should include constrained decode configs (top-p/top-k) in the CSV?

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_eval_prompts.csv (CSV of ~500 prompts + tag columns)

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
https://redwood.inference/docs
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme-ai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next steps

Marissa — thanks, that recap is perfect. A few quick answers and requests: 

- Comparator runs: Dana (copied) will run the side-by-side tests against Hyperscaler X and Y. She’ll need the prompt CSV and the suggested decode configs.
- Hallucination tests: please include a short subset (20 prompts) flagged as "hard factual" and one flagged as "source-attribute" so we can measure hallucination rates vs our internal ground truth.
- Regs: Low-latency is not necessary for this run. Our emphasis is on MRR/precision of facts and avoiding evasive outputs.

Availability: Dana and I are available Tue 4/20 between 9–11am PT for the live side-by-side. If that works, we can lock it now.

One more thing — can Rishi include an explanation of any differences we should expect when running against your hosted API vs the hyperscaler managed endpoints (e.g., tokenization, stop-sequence behavior, or fallback variants)? That will help us interpret any small discrepancies.

Thanks,
Alex

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 10:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 
> 
> - Recap: you’re validating model quality ...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next steps

Alex / Dana — thanks for the quick reply. Attached is the CSV of eval prompts (redwood_vs_hyperscalers_eval_prompts.csv). A few notes on contents and decode configs: 

- CSV contains: prompt_id, prompt_text, difficulty_tag (easy/medium/hard), fact_check_reference_id, expected_output_snippet. We flagged 20 hard factual prompts under difficulty_tag=hard and added a source-attribute column where appropriate.
- Suggested decode configs column: we included recommended temperature (0.0 for strict factual checks, 0.2 for open-ended), top_p (0.9), and recommended max_tokens per prompt.
- Repro tips: include identical stop sequences and normalize whitespace before computing token-level diffs.

Rishi — can you run the initial 500-sample regression check on our hosted endpoint today and share the PDF? Please include an explanation of likely tokenization differences and any server-side safety filters that might impact outputs (we should call these out so Acme can control for them).

Proposed schedule: Tue 4/20 9:30–10:15am PT for the side-by-side (45m). Alex / Dana, if that works, I’ll send calendar invite with a short agenda (1) go over regression PDF (2) run 3–4 representative prompts live (3) discuss config alignment and next rollout steps).

Thanks — attaching the CSV and linking a Drive folder for results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-results

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_eval_prompts.csv

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme-ai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next steps

Alex / team — ran the initial regression checks against our hosted endpoint this morning. Summary highlights (full detail in attached PDF): 

- Sample size: 500 prompts (matching CSV). Overall factuality precision was 93% on our scoring heuristic; hallucination rate (defined per agreed rubric) was ~4.6%.
- Known diffs vs hyperscaler endpoints: tokenization edge-cases (emoji, non-ascii punctuation) can cause small output shifts; we document normalization steps in section 2 of the PDF.
- Safety filters: our hosted endpoint applies a light safety post-filter which primarily affects open-ended, unsafe generations; for strict factual checks (temperature=0.0) the impact is negligible but we call it out so you can disable it in a private deployment test if needed.

Attached: initial_regression_checks.pdf (includes per-prompt pass/fail, example outputs, and a short FAQ on interpreting diffs).

Confirmed: Tue 4/20 9:30–10:15am PT looks good for Marissa, Alex, Dana, and Rishi. I’ll send the calendar invite and include a brief agenda and hubspot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
